The election process was characterized by low attendance numbers, record high amounts of ballots spoiled by the voters, and a plethora of violations (all violent instances coded separately), including but not limited to: vote buying, pressuring of independent and opposition election monitors, ballot throw-ins, process violations, etc. The severity of violations varied from region to region, the recorded instances, and the overall atmosphere surrounding the process led many local monitoring groups to conclude that the elections were fabricated by the government. As for the results, all 19 heads of regions running for reelection stayed in power, some with 'record high numbers'. For legislative committee elections, the ruling United Russia party won the house majority in every region, with either LDPR or KPRF (both considered controlled opposition) taking second places. Independent candidates or candidates from parties other than ER managed to win only in a few minor elections (eg. mayoral).
